signature.name: First-Screen Conversion
signature.description: Before the first scroll, does the page say what it does and for whom, show real output, show the path to a first result, and does that path actually work, by design of the SKILL.md rather than luck?

group-a.signature_why: Plain what-sentence, the exact clone/demo/open block and a real report capture all fit on the first screen, and a scripted first-screen gate makes it repeatable; but the opener drops 'sales' and never says who it is for.
group-a.loved: Receipts all the way down: selftest passes 77/77 with 18/18 seeded lies caught on my machine, and the README says outright that the report's quotes come from a prepared sample and the tool runs no model.
group-a.docked: The hero crop is the report's generic header and stat cards, the least telling part of the output, and a newcomer has to infer the sales-coaching audience.

group-b.signature_why: What-sentence and quickstart are on the first screen, but the proof there is a rebuilt animation of real strings rather than a capture, it paints an almost empty box at 0.5s, and the real report capture sits below the fold.
group-b.loved: The input -> check -> output Reel uses real data, ties a transcript line to its verification and the 'Quote verified' result, and ships light and dark SVGs at about 4.5 KB each.
group-b.docked: The body is mostly the repo's own README reshuffled, 'Who it fits' never names a reader, it ends on a process-leak line ('were not run for this page (unverified)'), and the demo breaks the skill's own ladder rule to put the real captured output first.

group-c.signature_why: Best what+who sentence of the three ('For people who review sales or customer calls') with a real report crop above the fold and the Try it heading visible, though the commands themselves start just below the first screen.
group-c.loved: It explains the non-obvious hook exactly as the code does it (case- and punctuation-insensitive substring within one turn), and it caught whisper-cli from run.py where the repo's own docs only say whisper.cpp.
group-c.docked: Two of the three transcript lines are cut off in a horizontally scrolling code block right above the hero, and a 'How this README was checked' footer is process residue a maintainer would delete.
